record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Singularities of Mappings
record.original_question: In Damon's fibre-square method, let f=i^*(F) be obtained from a stable unfolding F by a transverse fibre product with a map i, let D be the image or discriminant of F, and let T^1_rel be the relative cokernel theta(I)/(tI(theta_{C^p x C^d / C^d}) + I^*(Der(-log D))) for a deformation I of i. In the image case p=n+1, is T^1_rel always Cohen-Macaulay of grade p for the weighted homogeneous germs relevant to Mond's conjecture, equivalently making the push-forward of T^1_rel to the base free and forcing mu_I = A_e-codimension?

evidence.quote: for a weighted homogeneous germ, muI = Ae-codimension if and only if pi*(T1rel) is free
conjecture 1.5 is equivalent to the statement that T1rel is Cohen Macaulay of grade p.
But why should this hold in general?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F:(\mathbb{C}^N,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^P,0)$ be a stable map-germ, regarded as a stable unfolding, and let $D\subset(\mathbb{C}^P,0)$ be its image (in the image case) or discriminant. Let $\mathrm{Der}(-\log D)$ denote the module of germs of vector fields on $(\mathbb{C}^P,0)$ tangent to $D$. Let $i:(\mathbb{C}^d,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^P,0)$ be a map-germ transverse to $F$ in the sense of Damon's fibre-square construction, so that $f=i^{*}(F):(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ is obtained as the transverse fibre product. Consider a deformation $I:(\mathbb{C}^d\times\mathbb{C}^s,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^P\times\mathbb{C}^s,0)$ of $i$ over a parameter space $(\mathbb{C}^s,0)$, and form the relative module
$$T^{1}_{\mathrm{rel}} \;=\; \theta(I)\big/\bigl(tI(\theta_{\mathbb{C}^p\times\mathbb{C}^d/\mathbb{C}^d}) + I^{*}(\mathrm{Der}(-\log D))\bigr),$$
where $\theta(I)$ is the module of vector fields along $I$ and $tI$ denotes the relative tangent map.

Assume we are in the image case $p=n+1$ and that $f$ is a weighted homogeneous germ of the type relevant to the Mond conjecture (i.e. an $\mathcal{A}$-finite germ admitting a one-parameter stable unfolding, in nice dimensions). Denote by $\pi$ the projection from the total space of the deformation to the parameter base, by $\mu_I(f)$ the image Milnor number of $f$, and by $\mathcal{A}_e\text{-codim}(f)$ its $\mathcal{A}_e$-codimension.

Question: Is $T^{1}_{\mathrm{rel}}$ always Cohen–Macaulay of grade $p$ for such weighted homogeneous germs, equivalently is the push-forward $\pi_{*}(T^{1}_{\mathrm{rel}})$ a free $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^s,0}$-module, and does this therefore force the equality $\mu_I(f)=\mathcal{A}_e\text{-codim}(f)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Mond's conjecture remains open in general. Recent work establishes only weak or partial versions, e.g. a "weak Mond conjecture" (Giménez Conejero–Nuño-Ballesteros, 2023), proofs for restricted settings such as maps between curves (Ament, 2017), wave fronts (2024), and conditional results showing the conjecture holds when certain Jacobian-type modules are Cohen–Macaulay. No source verifies the general Cohen–Macaulay property of the relative module $T^1_{\mathrm{rel}}$ of grade $p$ for all weighted homogeneous germs in the image case.

status_evidence.title: A weak version of the Mond conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes a weak version of Mond's conjecture, indicating the full conjecture is not yet proved.
status_evidence.claim: Mond's conjecture is still open in general; only a weak version is established.

status_evidence.title: A Jacobian module for disentanglements and applications to Mond's conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: If a certain Jacobian/relative module is Cohen-Macaulay then Mond's conjecture holds.
status_evidence.claim: Cohen-Macaulayness of the relevant relative module is known to imply Mond's conjecture, but is not established in general.

status_evidence.title: A proof of the Mond conjecture for wave fronts
status_evidence.snippet: Proof in the special wave front case, indicating general case remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Only special-case proofs exist; general statement remains open.
